utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. McCloskey, you can ask General Krstic what he means when he says "urban areas" exactly, and he will provide an answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you include suburbs in your definition of urban areas?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, the enclave of Srebrenica is made up of hundreds of villages, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know how many villages there are, but quite a few that were part of the enclave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. McCloskey, sorry to interrupt you, but I think that this would be a convenient time for our break, so we will have a 15-minute break at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Having fulfilled our city habits for a break, we can continue, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: General Krstic, could you step briefly to the map which is Exhibit 485, that large map in front of you, and I believe there was a big pen someone had earlier, and could you draw the area on the Srebrenica enclave that you feel is the urban area. And I can tell you that the map that you're looking at, 485, is based on the NATO maps that you're familiar with and of the same and is to scale, and you can see down at the bottom a scale of kilometres. It doesn't need to be exact, certainly, but can you just draw an area that you feel is the urban area as defined by this order, Krivaja 95?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Petrusic, you have an objection to make?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. The Defence considers that possibly the answer to this question can be given, that is to say, indicated on the map on Exhibit number 2, where the places are quoted and the areas shown. They are far clearer on that map, on that exhibit, than they are on this map that my learned colleague is talking about, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Petrusic. In any case, we can try. If General Krstic tells us that it is easier for him to respond by using the Exhibit number 2, then we can perhaps replace it, take off this particular exhibit and allow General Krstic to use the other exhibit. So Mr. McCloskey knows this. He knows about the exhibit. Thank you for your suggestion, but let us try.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: They're both good maps. We could do both, but, General, do you have any problems marking 385 [sic] the big NATO-based map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At all events, the other map would be better, I think. On this map, you can only see the names of several places. It is very difficult to indicate it on this map. I can just give you an approximation and show you the line that the Corps Commander's order referred to, the line to be taken up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: There may be miscommunication. I'm not asking you to make actual references to the trig points and the various objectives on the map. That's not what I'm asking. I'm just merely asking for the urban area of the Srebrenica enclave, and if that could be done on either map, I don't really care. I think I misspoke. The big map in front of us is 458, not 385. But I'm not asking for a military analysis of the objectives and all that. That's not what I'm asking. Now, if there is no such thing as the urban area or if there's something that can't be explained here, please tell me, General, but -- and either map is fine.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The line where the forces of the Drina Corps were to have reached, that is to say, the orders of the Corps Commander, on this map would be the following -- I haven't got the names of the places indicated here though, but I will show you. I think that Banja Guber is somewhere around here. Zivkovo Brdo lies somewhere in this region. Then we have Alibegovac and Kak.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What about Gradac? Actually, General, maybe I can save us some time. I don't want, at this point, to get into the various objectives that you're talking about. I just wanted you to show us where you believe the urban areas are, the urban area of Srebrenica. The order says, "Reduce them to their urban areas." "Reducing the size of the enclave to Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. their urban areas." Are you saying that's basically the same as the military objective or is that different? If it's the same as the military objective, fine. If not, can you tell us roughly where the urban area for Srebrenica is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In respect to what the Commander ordered, that is to say, the line we were to reach, you can see clearly that all the other villages in the protected zone were not urban areas. The urban area of Srebrenica, it is difficult for me to define, but I think that what the suburbs are -- that the suburbs belong to the urban area, the outskirts. Here we have the village of Bojna, somewhere in this part. Then we have Bajramovici, Pusulici. All that are the outskirts. Then we have Potocari. That too, Potocari too, because they are linked up with the main road and it's all inhabited area. From Srebrenica to Potocari, that makes up a whole. It doesn't go up to Potocari alone, but goes up to the Zuti Most area, the Yellow Bridge area, which is where the checkpoint was while the forces of the Dutch Battalion were present in the area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. McCloskey, the General has already said that it would be easier for him to answer your question with the other exhibit. So, Mr. Usher, perhaps we should remove this map and let the General respond in the way that is best suited for him. General, the idea of this question was that there was a zone that was to be protected, the protected area of Srebrenica, and there was a military objective of the operation which was to reduce those areas to their urban boundaries. Mr. McCloskey wants to know what is, in your opinion, this urban area which was indicated as the objective of the military operation. Mr. Usher, could you please give us the map which will enable General Krstic to respond to the question put to him by Mr. McCloskey. Now, Mr. McCloskey, will you please ask your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: General, if you could put -- just draw the boundaries of the urban areas as -- that you feel are the urban areas as defined in this order; just the boundaries, if you could. Take some time to study it, but ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do apologise, and I have to repeat what I've already said. First, the objective of this operation was not the civilian population but the forces of the 28th Division. The Corps Commander ordered the line, the demarcation line of Srebrenica and Zepa, and which line the forces were to reach, attain. And it is correct to say that in his order, the line Banja Guber, Zivko Brdo, Alibegovac, and the Kak feature, that was it. And from his decision, we can see that if we were to take up positions along this line, that all the rest does not belong to the urban area of Srebrenica, neither was it our intention to attack further on towards Srebrenica. I do not know the mayor of Srebrenica, when it comes to the status of the town, what the urban area actually implies and what is defined as the urban area, but I can say that everything within this, east of Srebrenica position to the demarcation line, that all that was the urban area, towards Bratunac, the Zuti Most, from Srebrenica, and Potocari. That is an urban area and it is all linked up. It is one entity. And then to the west, towards Viogora and several other villages; and to the south, the village of Bojna, Pusulici, and Bajramovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you do a boundary of the urban area for Srebrenica, just with -- and if you don't feel like you can, that's fine; we'll go on to the next question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, all I can do is to draw in what I have indicated, to draw it in.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And if you could just mark your initials on that so we can identify it for the record, on the red line you've drawn. Okay. Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. McCloskey, I'm sorry to interrupt you. General Krstic, if we look at the line that you have just drawn, I should like to know if that line involved certain modifications in the boundaries of the Srebrenica protected area.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So this means that for the purposes of the Krivaja 95 operation, one of the objectives was to reduce this area to its urban boundaries but not to modify the lines, to change the lines that you have indicated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The objective of the operation of Krivaja 95 was not at all to advance towards this line or circle that I have drawn in here and indicated. The objective was the line that was quoted in the order. Perhaps that was unfortunately written down in the order by the Corps Commander, because someone might have thought that if you advanced towards this line, that it is an urban line. It is the line referred to in the order by the Corps Commander, and that's where the difference lies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Sorry, Mr. McCloskey. You may -- I'm sorry. Madam Judge Wald.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. McCloskey. General, did the lines that you indicated on the map there, are they different from the lines that had been defined a couple of years earlier by the UN when it declared Srebrenica a protected enclave? In short, let me put it another way: Were there DutchBat patrols, DutchBat OPs or posts outside of the line that you drew there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Madam Judge, these are not the lines of the protected area. Let me repeat once again: It was not our objective to advance towards the line that I have indicated here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: I understand, General. I just wanted to know -- I just wanted to clarify the relationship between the line that you drew and what had been included in the UN protected enclave. I understand that was not your objective, and you've answered my question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: General, there is on that same page, there is an area entitled "Objective." It says: "By a surprise attack, to separate and reduce in size the Srebrenica and Zepa enclaves." I think we've talked about that a bit, but I want to ask you about this next part: "To improve the tactical position of the forces in the depth of the area and to create conditions for the elimination of the enclaves." Now, in particular, I want you to tell the Court, what is meant by "creating conditions," first, and then "for the elimination of the enclave"? What does that mean: "creating conditions for the elimination of the enclave"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It means -- that is to say, it's another time. It implied another time. If the forces of the 28th Division were to continue to do what they had been doing throughout the time since the beginning of the operation, then perhaps a new operation and the planning of a new operation would be undertaken. So within this operation, that was not at all our objective.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What were the conditions that were supposed to be created that would -- that could lead in the future to the elimination of the enclaves? It says "create conditions," and that's the present. What does that create -- what conditions are to be created by this order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: By advancing to the line referred to in the order by the corps commander -- and that is the line Banja Guber, Zivko Brdo, Alibegovac, Kak -- no conditions had been created for the elimination of the enclaves, first of all, because it was a protected zone, a protected area, and because there was the civilian population there. And it was not at all our intention to continue the attack towards Srebrenica, and I have already spoken about that at length in the examination-in-chief. And I should like to repeat: To create conditions, that refers to some other time. Only if the forces of the 28th Division continue doing what they had been doing up until then.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: General, it is the submission of the Prosecution that the term "urban areas" refers to the city areas of Srebrenica, and that creating a condition for the elimination of the enclave meant you were to create a situation where the enclave is now bordered by the urban area. Do you contest this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The order by the Commander of the Drina Corps -- this is not seen at all from the order of the Drina Corps Commander when he said advance to such-and-such a line and create conditions for the elimination of the enclaves. Let me repeat, that is some other time, a later point in time, only if there was repeated occurrence of what had happened in the operations of the 28th Division. The Drina Corps had no other plans, nor did it elaborate any document whatsoever for it to be able to realise the operation, that is to say, to eliminate the enclave. All that existed were several documents of which we have the order by the Commander for the separation of the Zepa and Srebrenica enclave. Then there was a reconnaissance plan, communications plan, and the plan for quartermaster affairs. And had the objective been the elimination of the enclaves, then the Commander of the Drina Corps would have had to have undertaken the elaboration of all other documents and plans focusing on logistics, focusing on quartermaster issues for the population, a plan for cooperation with the civilian structures, a plan for cooperation with UNPROFOR and all the other documents that this would require. And the Drina Corps Command did not have that. It did not devise plans of this kind, neither did it consider that for the implementation of this order by the Drina Corps plans of that kind were at all necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we could go to Exhibit 425A briefly, the Main Staff of the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. McCloskey, before we start analysing this particular exhibit, I have to interrupt you once again, and I'm sorry for that. General Krstic, the term -- the words "to reduce to urban areas," even if your definition which would include suburbs, in view those words, I should like to know what were the consequences as regards the modification of the boundaries of the protected zone, one thing. And second, what were the consequences as regards the status of the observation posts and checkpoints which were manned at the time by the members of the Dutch Battalion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I apologise. I did not quite catch your first question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm referring to the objective of the Krivaja 95 operation. One objective was to reduce the areas, the zones, to their urban areas. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, what I should like to know is the following: What were the consequences of that for the boundaries of the protected area? So that is one question. And my second question was: What were the consequences for the observation posts that were manned by members of the Dutch Battalion at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With respect to your first question, Your Honour, vital changes with respect to the boundaries of the protected area did not exist nor would the realisation of this decision by the Commander lead to any serious repercussions and upset the boundaries of the protected zone, protected area. So in the area of Zeleni Jadar, that would remain within the protected zone area. Moving to Zivkovo Brdo, the protected area would be somewhat moved, shifted. In the Alibegovac and Kak feature, the boundaries would remain practically the same because the valley from the Zeleni Jadar, from the south and the south-west, would be the boundary there. In between the valley of Zeleni Jadar and the Kak feature and Alibegovac, there were known inhabited areas. There were previously, but there were no inhabitants there. There were Serbian villages there and Bosniak villages there as well. At some earlier date they were burnt, so there were no inhabitants there at the time. The village of Podravanje, which was outside the protected area, was not inhabited either by Serbs or Muslims, Bosniaks, but the forces of the 28th Division held the village. They were in the village. As to your second question, Your Honour, vital changes, there were hardly any. There would be hardly any vital changes in shifting for the reconnaissance points, observation points, the OPs of the Dutch Battalion. In Zeleni Jadar, the checkpoint would remain, the OP would remain. And in the Alibegovac and Kak feature, the UNPROFOR OP would also remain. And I remember during our reconnaissance we noticed a point between Alibegovac and Kakanj from the southern side, and that too would remain on that particular line, the line where the forces of the Drina Corps were to advance from the south.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, General. Mr. McCloskey, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, I just want to briefly --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I just want to briefly go to the directive 7, and if I could direct your attention to the paragraph entitled the "Drina Corps."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. McCloskey, could you please tell us once again the number of the exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. It's Exhibit 425A, and the B/C/S version, it should be shortly after "Unit Assignments" at paragraph 5, and then it gives Corps and you'll see the Drina Corps mentioned there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, if you would take a moment to read the first paragraph, which is the paragraph that I'm most concerned about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Once again, Mr. McCloskey, I have to interrupt you. Could you please be more specific in terms of references so that the usher can give us the relevant text and the relevant paragraph on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. President. It's page 10 in the English. And the B/C/S, I believe the General has found it based on my explanation. I'm sorry, I forgot about the English. It's at the bottom of the page under "Drina Corps." There we go. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: General, when you've had a chance to look at that first paragraph, I'd like to ask you a question or two about it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That refers to the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. Just that first paragraph of the "Drina Corps" in the directive. Now, you stated earlier that you did have a chance to review this document, Exhibit 425, and the military document associated it, which was directive 7/1. What I'd like to ask you about is the middle part of it, where it says: "... while in the direction of the Srebrenica and Zepa enclaves, complete physical separation of Srebrenica from Zepa should be carried out as soon as possible, preventing even communication between individuals in the two enclaves." Now, that sounds like the first objective in Krivaja 95, the separation of the two enclaves. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the next part of the directive reads, and I quote: "By planned and well-thought-out combat operations create an unbearable situation of total insecurity with no hope of further survival or life for the inhabitants of Srebrenica and Zepa." Was this last part that I just read incorporated into the Krivaja 95 plan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. This was by no means included in the plan. We never took this into account. We never had any thoughts to this effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The outcome of the overall operation ended in the elimination of the Srebrenica enclave, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but later on I'm sure that we will see, and I have already discussed it, what the cause of that was, what were the reasons for that, and who was responsible for the continuation of the operation after the commanders in the area had reported on the successful completion of their assignment, their initial assignment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, let me ask you about -- if thousands of people from the Srebrenica enclave crowded into the city areas of Srebrenica, what kind of conditions would that create for those people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After the decision of the Drina Corps Commander for active operation, active combat activity, with the purpose of separating Zepa and Srebrenica, was carried out, nothing in particular would have changed in the life of the citizens of Srebrenica. We didn't target the civilian population of Srebrenica at all. At that time, the objective wasn't even the 28th Division. The main objective at the time was to prevent their communication and their infiltrations into the no man's land between Srebrenica and Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could all the inhabitants of the Srebrenica enclave fit into the city area of Srebrenica and live in any kind of a decent way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Let me just answer to the question relating to the line that was taken up by the Drina Corps forces. Again, I have to say that nothing would have changed. The line that I have drawn on the map is -- well, I'm not going to call it an arbitrary line, but it may fall within the boundaries of the urban area. I hope I did answer your question. The objective of the Drina Corps forces was not to penetrate the area within this circle, according to the decision -- to the order of the Corps Commander. We didn't deploy any forces from the north, the west, nor from most of the parts of the eastern area. This could be seen from the documents and the orders that have been produced during my examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could thousands of people live in the Srebrenica urban areas?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As regards the line that I have drawn on the map, of course they couldn't. However, this line here has nothing to do with what I have previously spoken about, that is, the line that was supposed to be taken up by the Drina Corps forces, which, according to some, were actually the boundaries of some urban area. Because from the east and partly from the north, that is, the area between Srebrenica and onwards, that was already the urban area from the moment Srebrenica was declared a safe area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm going to direct your attention now to page 14 in the English. It should be paragraph 6, called "Support for Combat Operations" in the B/C/S, the fourth paragraph down, beginning "The relevant state." Paragraph 6 in the B/C/S, General. You should be able to follow them by paragraphs. It's entitled "Support for Combat Operations" in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You said page 14?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry. That's the English. You have to go by the paragraph for the B/C/S. So if you could just try to find paragraph -- what is marked as heading or paragraph 6, "Support for Combat Operation." It looks like page 10 in your copy, General.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And if you could review paragraph 4, starting with "The relevant state and military organs," and if you could just read that to yourself for a moment and then I'll ask you something about it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So under the heading "Support for Combat Operations" and then the subheading "Moral and Psychological Support," this paragraph says: "The relevant state and military organs responsible for work with UNPROFOR and humanitarian organisations shall, through the planned and unobtrusively restrictive issuing of permits, reduce and limit the logistics support of UNPROFOR to the enclaves and the supply of material resources to the Muslim population, making them dependent on our goodwill while at the same time avoiding condemnation by the International Community and international public opinion." The effect of this order would be reducing the amount of food that goes to the civilian population; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that the best would be for me not to comment on this at all. One can clearly see that this is not a military document, properly speaking, but a political document which had nothing to do with the Drina Corps Command.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Who enforced whether convoys got into the Srebrenica enclave or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it is difficult for me to say who did that, whether to allow them in or not. The MUP forces were also there in the area, and the checkpoints at the border of the enclave were manned by the members of the army. So whether a convoy would be allowed in or not, I didn't have any responsibility for that. I couldn't issue any decisions to that effect. I don't know about General Zivanovic. All I know is that could have been decided upon only by the Main Staff VRS and the Supreme Command, because all affairs concerning UNPROFOR were conducted at those levels, in particular in respect of the supplies of the enclaves, not only Srebrenica and Zepa enclaves but the enclave of Gorazde and others. So the Drina Corps Command did not guide itself in any way for its operations by anything that was said here in this directive which was issued by the Supreme Command.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Is the Drina Corps responsible for carrying out the orders of the Supreme Command as it comes down to you through the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the Drina Corps had to carry out the orders. But specifically speaking, when it comes to this particular paragraph, I don't know. It's very difficult to comment on this. Only the liaison officer of the Main Staff was able, on the basis of their decisions, to allow or deny entry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I note we've just gone by 3.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. McCloskey. We have worked five minutes more, at least. We have a lot of work to do, but I think that we have to wind up for the day -- we have a number of other obligations, the Chamber -- and we will be here again at 20 minutes past 9.00 to continue with the cross-examination. I'll see you tomorrow.
